title: European Stocks in Focus as Bekaert Jumps 8% on Q3 Sales
summary: European stocks in focus: Bekaert rose over 8% on Q3 sales, Fincantieri and Exosens gained on defense orders and Elia lifted its 2026 profit guidance.

## Fincantieri Rises Nearly 6% on €500 Million Navy Contract


Per[Investing.com](https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/fincantieri-wins-500m-navy-contract-shares-rise-6-93CH-5053180) , shares in Italian shipbuilder Fincantieri (BIT:FCT) rose nearly 6% on Friday after the company secured a contract worth around €500 million ($549 million) to build a third logistic support ship for the Italian Navy.


A temporary group of companies led by Fincantieri, with participation from Leonardo (BIT:LDOF), signed the contract on Thursday with OCCAR, the European defense procurement agency, the report said.


## Exosens Jumps More Than 6% on Bundeswehr Night Vision Order


Exosens shares jumped more than 6% on Friday after the company won an order to supply 6,000 5G image intensifier tubes to Germany's Future Soldier program, known as IdZ-ES,[Investing.com](https://au.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/exosens-shares-jump-6-on-german-army-night-vision-order-93CH-4798697) reported. The tubes will be integrated into fused night vision binoculars used by Bundeswehr infantry soldiers, with deliveries set to begin in early 2027 and continue over several years.


Rheinmetall leads the IdZ-ES program as prime contractor, according to the same report. Exosens CEO Jérôme Cerisier said the order "demonstrates the growing adoption of our 5G technology among European armed forces."

## Elia Raises 2026 Net Profit Guidance to €730-760 Million


Elia raised its 2026 net profit guidance across all divisions and at the group level in its third-quarter trading update on Friday, per[Investing.com](https://ca.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/elia-raises-2026-net-income-guidance-across-all-divisions-93CH-4983114) . The new range of €730-760 million compares with a prior range of €690-740 million and includes a negative impact of approximately €65 million, mainly related to impairments on US investments. The report did not state how Elia's shares traded.


In Belgium, the ETB unit now targets net profit of €330-340 million, helped by a Belgian 10-year OLO rate of 3.8% against a prior assumption of 3.4%. In Germany, the adjusted net profit target rose to €630-650 million from €585-625 million, based on a regulatory base rate of 3.3% instead of 3.0%. The non-regulated segment and Nemo Link are now expected to contribute €15-25 million versus a prior expectation of break-even, while 2026 capital expenditure stays at approximately €6.5 billion, around €1.7 billion in Belgium and €4.8 billion in Germany, according to the same report.
